blockers.evidence:
Severity: major. Location: packages/rigorloop/test/cli-observability.test.js:572, T05 rotates only above the exact byte boundary and retains four archives (threshold setup/expected size at lines 585, 589, 599; retention assertions at lines 606–616). CLI's Local diagnostic logging contract requires rotation only above 5 MiB and active plus four archives. The exact-size test instead derives its inputs and expected size from production MAX_LOG_BYTES. The retention test verifies that names 0–4 remain and that archive4 contains former archive3, but never excludes archive5 or any extra retained member.
Independent controlled reproduction copied only this native file, package module metadata and its three runtime dependencies into an automatically cleaned private directory; no repository runtime source was changed. Replacing the production 5 MiB constant with 4 MiB leaves all 30 logging-core cases passing. Separately adding rigorloop.5.jsonl to LOG_NAMES and moving the rotation oldest/index bounds to five archives also leaves all 30 cases passing. Unmodified control passes 30. Thus both explicit contract violations remain invisible despite the named boundary test. Adjacent event-size protection is independent: reducing MAX_EVENT_BYTES from 16 KiB to 8 KiB fails exactly T02's literal 16 KiB assertion; no event-limit correction is requested.
The identity-stable strict regression is /tmp/rigorloop-suite-organization-work/probe_m8_rotation_contract.py, sha256:5f7b3d7af37c3994fe01066245875c5dc4acb15940bc2bba2a9f8a8366c487db. Run python /tmp/rigorloop-suite-organization-work/probe_m8_rotation_contract.py before (or after/current to retain separate logs). It runs the exact existing named native case under Node TAP in each independently mutated private copy. It succeeds only if each mutant exits1, runs exactly one case, and fails that named case through ERR_ASSERTION; a setup/import error or wrong case does not satisfy it. On this subject both mutant native runs exit0 and the strict regression exits1. Detailed outputs are m8-rotation-contract-before.json and the two named TAP logs; broader diagnostic experiments are m8-review-rotation-limit-probe.json and m8-review-adjacent-limits.json.
This is a demonstrated test-oracle defect, not evidence that the current product uses a wrong limit. It is recorded during independently authorized M8 review preparation. The exact final M8 handoff and required integrated proof are still pending, so this reviewer-owned blocker records the concrete required correction without asserting a completed formal M8 judgment. Other reviewed M8 source groups have no preliminary material concern. No implementation, activity, work or another actor's evidence was changed by the reviewer.
